hints: Look at how the repeat unit is linked, carbon to carbon with no small molecule lost, so think about which type of polymerisation this is.
For this type of polymerisation the monomer must contain a C=C double bond, which opens up to form the two new single bonds in the chain.
Compare the side groups on the repeat unit, a $\text{CH}_3$ and a $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, with the options and keep the one that has both groups attached to the same C=C carbon.
walkthrough:
**Recognise addition polymerisation**

PMMA has an all-carbon backbone with no ester or amide link in the main chain. That tells you it is an addition polymer, made from an alkene monomer.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{alkene monomer } \text{C=C} \rightarrow \text{repeat unit } \text{-C-C-}$$

**Work backwards from repeat to monomer**

To find the monomer, take one repeat unit and change the two chain bonds back into a double bond. The $\text{-CH}_2\text{-}$ becomes $\text{CH}_2=$ and the $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(CO}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)-}$ becomes $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)(CO}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)}=$.

So the monomer must be:
$$\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{C(CH}_3\text{)(CO}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)}$$

**Check the ester side chain**

The repeat unit carries $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is a methyl ester, not a carboxylic acid $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. So the monomer must also be the methyl ester.

That gives methyl 2-methylprop-2-enoate, commonly called methyl methacrylate, which matches the correct choice.

options.A: Incorrect. This is 2-methylpropanoic acid, a saturated carboxylic acid with no C=C bond. It cannot undergo addition polymerisation, and it has $\text{OH}$ instead of the $\text{OCH}_3$ ester group seen in PMMA.
options.B: Incorrect. This does have the correct C=C bond and the $\text{CH}_3$ branch, but it is methacrylic acid with $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. PMMA needs the methyl ester $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, so this would give poly(methacrylic acid), not PMMA.
options.C: Incorrect. This has the correct methyl ester group $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, but it is saturated with single bonds only. Without a C=C double bond it cannot act as an addition monomer. This is a common trap if you only match the ester group.
options.D: Correct. This is $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{C(CH}_3\text{)CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, methyl methacrylate. The C=C opens on polymerisation to give $\text{-CH}_2\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(CO}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)-}$, exactly the repeat unit shown.
